requirements.summary: A Monitor-owned root scheduler bounds hostile Domain execution and eventually selects another eligible guaranteed Domain without trusting Linux selector state.
Global Domain identity scales beyond a bounded per-CPU resident slot set without alias, stale generation use, unsafe eviction, or starvation of guaranteed Domains.
Every syscall, exception, IRQ, NMI-class entry, nested entry, and return preserves the active Domain, MemoryView, epoch, stack, and per-CPU ownership invariants.
Shared executable kernel content is Monitor-verified, read-only, W^X, versioned, and updated only through an authority-checked cross-view transaction.
Every mutable privileged page is Domain-private, typed-service-owned, Monitor-owned, or an explicitly shared typed buffer; unknown ownership is unmapped.
Arbitrary service Domain compromise is bounded by typed endpoints, caller-frozen authority intersection, explicit buffers, budgets, and Monitor receipts.
Offline roots, online management, node Monitors, recovery, and key rotation have explicit trust and compromise boundaries.
Signed bounded leases remain safe under partitions, delayed or reordered messages, local clock assumptions, fencing, restart, migration, and namespace recovery.
Component assumptions, guarantees, owned state, visible actions, and refinement mappings compose into the hostile-kernel top-level claim.
Process-through-container Domain granularity has an explicit security and complete-path cost envelope against container, KVM, and microVM baselines.
Positive assurance decisions consume validator-owned immutable captured bytes and retain raw evidence with transitive provenance.
